WPFTweaksActivity.Description: Stops Windows from publishing or uploading user activities while preserving clipboard history.

WPFTweaksHiber.Description: Hibernation is really meant for laptops as it saves what's in memory before turning the PC off. It really should never be used.

WPFTweaksWidget.Description: Removes the annoying widgets in the bottom left of the Taskbar.
InvokeScript:
# Sometimes if you dont stop the Widgets process the removal may fail

      Get-Process *Widget* | Stop-Process
      Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.WidgetsPlatformRuntime -AllUsers | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers
      Get-AppxPackage MicrosoftWindows.Client.WebExperience -AllUsers | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers

      Invoke-WinUtilExplorerUpdate -action "restart"
      Write-Host "Removed widgets"

WPFTweaksRevertStartMenu.Description: Bring back the old Start Menu layout from before the gradual rollout of the new one in 25H2. On newer versions of Windows !!THIS TWEAK WILL NOT WORK!!

WPFTweaksDisableStoreSearch.Content: Microsoft Store Recommended Search Results - Disable
WPFTweaksDisableStoreSearch.Description: Will not display recommended Microsoft Store apps when searching for apps in the Start menu.

WPFTweaksServices.Description: Sets some services to Manual startup and adjusts the SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB registry value to better match system memory, which can significantly reduce the number of svchost.exe processes.

WPFTweaksServicesManual.Description: Sets MapsBroker and StorSvc to Manual startup if they still have their default startup type. Also adjusts SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB based on installed RAM. Undo restores the service startup types; the svchost registry adjustment is not reverted.

WPFTweaksServicesDisabled.Description: Disables Offline Files (CscService), Windows telemetry (DiagTrack) and Internet Connection Sharing (SharedAccess) when they have their original startup type. Undo restores their configured startup types. Do not enable this if you share this PC's Internet connection or use Offline Files.

WPFServiceGroupDiagnostics.Description: Expand the arrow to choose Windows diagnostic and telemetry services: diagnostic hosts, Diagnostic Policy Service, DiagTrack, Error Reporting and the Diagnostics Hub collector. Marking or unmarking only prepares changes; press Apply Tweaks to disable selected services or restore unchecked services. The main checkbox selects all available services. Disabling them stops Windows troubleshooters, problem detection and error reports.

WPFServiceGroupUseless.Description: Expand the arrow to choose optional Windows services. Marking or unmarking only prepares changes; press Apply Tweaks to disable selected services or restore unchecked services. The main checkbox selects all available services. Some support AutoPlay, device management or .NET networking. NetTcpPortSharing is often disabled by default; restoring it sets Manual startup.

WPFDriverGroupOptional.Description: Optional kernel drivers, NOT a recommended preset. Marking or unmarking only queues changes until Apply Tweaks, when driver disables require confirmation. Original startup settings are backed up for Undo. Boot/System and critical drivers are locked; missing drivers are hidden. Changes take effect after reboot and may affect media, networking or power monitoring. Does not delete .sys files. UCPD.sys remains a separate advanced tweak.

WPFToggleDriverTelemetry.Description: Optional Intel Telemetry driver on certain installations, not the Windows DiagTrack service. If its startup is already Disabled (as in some 20H2 images), APBOptimizer leaves it unchanged and cannot invent its previous state.

WPFToggleDriverPEAUTH.Description: Windows protected media authentication. Disabling may break DRM playback and protected media. Blocked if Boot/System/critical. Only change if you understand the side effects.

WPFToggleDriverTcpipreg.Description: Compatibility for software that reads legacy TCP/IP settings through the registry. This is not the main TCP/IP driver, but disabling can impair older networking applications. Boot/System startup is protected.

WPFToggleDriverIntelPMT.Description: Intel platform telemetry used by monitoring, management and potentially power/performance software. Can affect Intel OEM and tuning functions. Not necessarily unnecessary on Intel laptops.

WPFToggleDriverAppLockerFltr.Description: AppLocker application control filter. Disabling it can prevent AppLocker policy enforcement. Only available when installed and not protected by Boot/System startup or critical error handling. Original startup is saved for Undo; restart required.

WPFToggleDriverGpuEnergyDrv.Description: Windows GPU energy monitoring. Disabling may affect power telemetry and laptop efficiency. Separate from the graphics driver and not already present in this APBOptimizer catalog.

WPFToggleDriverIObitUnlocker.Description: Third-party IObit Unlocker driver. If you use its locked-file functions, disabling the driver can break them. Prefer uninstalling the unused application. Only available if the exact IObitUnlocker driver service exists.

WPFTweaksDisableUCPD.Description: Separate advanced tweak for the UserChoice Protection Driver. Protects browser/PDF default associations against unauthorized changes. Applying saves the original UCPD startup type and UCPD velocity scheduled-task state, then disables their next-boot startup. Undo restores both previous states. The task is disabled, not deleted. A reboot is required. Windows updates may reactivate the driver.

WPFToggleServiceWdiSystemHost.Description: Used by Windows Diagnostic Policy Service for system-level troubleshooting. Disabling it prevents some diagnostics from running. Undo restores Manual startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name WdiSystemHost -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name WdiSystemHost -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceWdiServiceHost.Description: Hosts diagnostics in the Local Service context. Disabling it prevents dependent troubleshooting from working. Undo restores Manual startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name WdiServiceHost -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name WdiServiceHost -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceDiagTrack.Description: Windows diagnostics and telemetry service. May already be disabled by Telemetry - Disable; Undo restores Automatic startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name DiagTrack -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name DiagTrack -ErrorAction Stop }
UndoScript: if ((Get-Service -Name DiagTrack -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Running') { Start-Service -Name DiagTrack -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceShellHWDetection.Description: Provides AutoPlay notifications when media or devices are connected. Disabling removes those notifications and can affect device-related features. Undo restores Automatic startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name ShellHWDetection -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name ShellHWDetection -ErrorAction Stop }
UndoScript: if ((Get-Service -Name ShellHWDetection -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Running') { Start-Service -Name ShellHWDetection -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceDPS.Description: Required for Windows problem detection and troubleshooting. Microsoft recommends keeping it enabled. Disabling can break diagnostics; Undo restores Automatic startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name DPS -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name DPS -ErrorAction Stop }
UndoScript: if ((Get-Service -Name DPS -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Running') { Start-Service -Name DPS -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceWMPNetworkSvc.Description: Shares Windows Media Player libraries with networked players and devices. Disabling removes that sharing. Undo restores Manual startup; this service may not exist on some Windows installations.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name WMPNetworkSvc -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name WMPNetworkSvc -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServicewisvc.Description: Used by the Windows Insider Program for preview builds. Disabling can interfere with Insider functionality. Undo restores Manual startup; the service may be absent.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name wisvc -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name wisvc -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceWerSvc.Description: Collects and reports Windows application and system failures. Disabling can reduce error reporting and diagnostic information. Undo restores Manual startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name WerSvc -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name WerSvc -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceFontCache3000.Description: Caches fonts for older Windows Presentation Foundation applications. Disabling may slow some .NET/WPF applications; often absent on newer Windows. Undo restores Manual startup.

WPFToggleServiceRetailDemo.Description: Used to display retail demonstration experiences on store devices. Disabling prevents retail demo functionality. Undo restores Manual startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name RetailDemo -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name RetailDemo -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceDiagnosticsHub.Description: Collects Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) events for diagnostic and development tools. Disabling can interfere with diagnostic traces and profiling. Undo restores Manual startup.

WPFToggleServiceDmwappushservice.Description: Routes device management push messages. Disabling can interrupt MDM/Intune management and device enrollment. Undo restores Manual startup.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name dmwappushservice -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name dmwappushservice -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceWhesvc.Description: Monitors device health for optimized Windows experiences. Disabling may affect device health and optimization features; it is not present on every Windows version. Undo restores Automatic startup and starts the service.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name whesvc -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name whesvc -ErrorAction Stop }
UndoScript: if ((Get-Service -Name whesvc -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Running') { Start-Service -Name whesvc -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFToggleServiceNetTcpPortSharing.Description: Allows Windows Communication Foundation applications to share TCP ports. This service is disabled on Windows by default; if already disabled, its checkbox starts checked. Unchecking sets Manual startup without starting it (required when using WCF port sharing).
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name NetTcpPortSharing -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name NetTcpPortSharing -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFTweaksDisableWindowsSearch.Description: Stops the Windows Search (WSearch) service and disables its startup. This reduces background indexing, but can slow or break file, Start menu and Outlook searches. Undo restores Automatic (Delayed Start) and starts the service.
InvokeScript: if ((Get-Service -Name WSearch -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Stopped') { Stop-Service -Name WSearch -ErrorAction Stop }
UndoScript: if ((Get-Service -Name WSearch -ErrorAction Stop).Status -ne 'Running') { Start-Service -Name WSearch -ErrorAction Stop }

WPFTweaksDisableSearchWebView2.Content: Start Search WebView2 Processes - Disable [restart required]
WPFTweaksDisableSearchWebView2.Description: Stops SearchHost.exe from keeping msedgewebview2.exe processes running in the background. Writes the same feature override as 'vivetool /disable /id:37926450' (SearchWebView2) directly to the registry, without running ViVeTool. Also turns off the new Start menu search interface. Microsoft can rename or remove this feature in an update, and then the override has no effect. Requires a restart. Undo removes the override.

WPFTweaksDisableEdgeBackground.Description: Disables Edge background mode and startup boost using Microsoft Edge policies. Does not remove Edge or the WebView2 runtime used by Teams and other apps. Undo removes both policy overrides.

WPFTaskGroupTelemetry.Description: Choose optional telemetry, compatibility, Windows Media Sharing and Firefox tasks in the dropdown. Marking or unmarking only stages changes; click Apply Tweaks to disable selected tasks or restore unchecked tasks previously managed by APBOptimizer. The master checkbox selects all manageable tasks. Missing tasks are hidden, and tasks disabled outside APBOptimizer are protected. Each task has an independent backup for Undo.

WPFToggleTaskCompatibilityAppraiser.Description: Collects application and device compatibility information. Disabling it can affect upgrade compatibility assessments. Undo restores the previously enabled state.

WPFToggleTaskProgramDataUpdater.Description: Updates program inventory data for application compatibility and diagnostics. Undo restores its original state.

WPFToggleTaskConsolidator.Description: Runs the Customer Experience Improvement Program data consolidation task. Undo restores its original state.

WPFToggleTaskUsbCeip.Description: Collects optional USB device usage diagnostics. Undo restores its original state.

WPFToggleTaskKernelCeip.Description: Collects optional Windows kernel experience data. Undo restores its original state.

WPFToggleTaskCompatibilityAppraiserExp.Description: Additional app compatibility telemetry task found on newer Windows installations. Disabling it may affect Windows upgrade compatibility assessments. Undo restores its previous state.

WPFToggleTaskWindowsMediaSharing.Description: Updates the Windows Media Player network-sharing library. Optional when you do not share media to devices on the local network; disabling may affect media library updates.

WPFToggleTaskUsageDataReporting.Description: Reports Windows FeatureConfig usage data. Disabling may affect feature usage reporting or internal feature configuration. Undo restores the previous state.

WPFToggleTaskSustainabilityTelemetry.Description: Reports Windows sustainability-related telemetry. Disabling may stop sustainability data collection. Does not disable PowerGridForecastTask.

WPFToggleTaskFirefoxDefaultBrowserAgent.Description: Optional Firefox task that checks default-browser changes. Matches only Mozilla's Firefox Default Browser Agent task(s) with a hexadecimal identifier; exact original states are saved for Undo. It does not disable Firefox updates.

WPFTweaksDisableTelemetryTasks.Description: Compatibility-only entry for older saved APBOptimizer configurations. The visible TaskGroup replaces this checkbox.

WPFTweaksPauseWindows2099.Description: Experimental registry-only pause through August 17, 2099. Microsoft officially supports pauses of up to 35 days, so this date may be ignored or reset. It is recommended to pause updates for 7 days in Windows Settings first, but this is not required. Applying saves the previous registry values; Undo restores them. It does not disable Windows services, scheduled tasks or rename protected DLLs. Blocks security updates if Windows honors the pause.

WPFTweaksDisableMemoryIntegrity.Description: Advanced Windows 10/11 option. Disables Memory integrity (HVCI) by setting the DeviceGuard HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity Enabled DWORD to 0, reducing protection against kernel malware. Requires administrator rights and a restart. It does NOT turn off all VBS, Credential Guard or the hypervisor. Policy-managed or UEFI-locked settings are protected; Windows may ignore or override registry changes. The original registry value (including an absent value) is backed up before applying and restored with Undo Selected Tweaks. Use Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation for the recommended manual method. Performance gains vary by hardware and game; none are guaranteed.

WPFTweaksDisablePowerThrottling.Description: Windows 10/11 power-management option. Sets HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerThrottling\PowerThrottlingOff (REG_DWORD) to 1 to turn off Windows process power throttling. It can help workloads that Windows throttles in the background, but usually does not improve foreground game FPS. Disabling energy-saving behavior may increase battery drain, power draw, temperature and fan noise. Requires administrator rights; a restart is recommended. Does not change the power plan, CPU limits or other power settings. Saves the exact original DWORD (including when absent) so Undo Selected Tweaks can restore it. A managed Windows policy may reapply this setting.

WPFTweaksDisableDevicePowerSaving.Content: USB Selective Suspend & PCIe Link State - Disable
WPFTweaksDisableDevicePowerSaving.Description: Windows 10/11 power plan option. Uses powercfg to set USB selective suspend and PCI Express Link State Power Management (ASPM) to Off for the plugged-in (AC) setting of the active power plan, then reactivates the plan. It can reduce USB mouse, controller or audio dropouts and PCIe wake-up latency; performance gains are not guaranteed. Battery (DC) values and other power plans are not changed. Power draw and idle temperature may increase slightly. Requires administrator rights; no restart needed. Saves the original AC values and the plan GUID so Undo Selected Tweaks can restore them.

WPFTweaksDisableCPUMitigations.Description: Advanced opt-in security setting for Windows 10/11. Follows shoober420/CPU_Mitigations.bat and Microsoft KB4073119: writes FeatureSettingsOverride=3 and FeatureSettingsOverrideMask=3 (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management. Disables operating-system speculative-execution mitigations including Spectre Variant 2 and Meltdown; other CPU, firmware and Windows protections are outside its scope. It substantially reduces security, especially on computers with untrusted applications or websites. Performance gains depend on CPU and workload and are not guaranteed. Requires administrator permissions and reboot. Saves both original registry values, including absent ones, so Undo Selected Tweaks can restore them. No third-party EXE or BAT is executed.

WPFTweaksBraveDebloat.Description: Disables various annoyances like Brave Rewards, Leo AI, Crypto Wallet and VPN.

WPFTweaksDisableWarningForUnsignedRdp.Description: Disables warnings shown when launching unsigned RDP files introduced with the latest Windows 10 and 11 updates.

WPFTweaksEdgeDebloat.Description: Disables various telemetry options, popups, and other annoyances in Edge.

WPFTweaksConsumerFeatures.Description: Stops promoted app installs and reduces app suggestions from Microsoft Store content.

InvokeScript:
# Disable Defender Auto Sample Submission (skipped when Defender is not installed)
      if (Get-Command Set-MpPreference -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Set-MpPreference -SubmitSamplesConsent 2 }

      # Disable (Connected User Experiences and Telemetry) Service
      Set-Service -Name diagtrack -StartupType Disabled

      # Disable (Windows Error Reporting Manager) Service; most Windows builds do not have it
      if (Get-Service -Name wermgr -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Set-Service -Name wermgr -StartupType Disabled }

      # Disable PowerShell 7 telemetry
      [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT', '1', 'Machine')

      Remove-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules" -Name PeriodInNanoSeconds -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
UndoScript:
# Enable Defender Auto Sample Submission (skipped when Defender is not installed)
      if (Get-Command Set-MpPreference -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Set-MpPreference -SubmitSamplesConsent 1 }

      # Enable (Connected User Experiences and Telemetry) Service
      Set-Service -Name diagtrack -StartupType Automatic

      # Enable (Windows Error Reporting Manager) Service; most Windows builds do not have it
      if (Get-Service -Name wermgr -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Set-Service -Name wermgr -StartupType Automatic }

      # Enable PowerShell 7 telemetry
      [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT', '', 'Machine')

WPFTweaksDeliveryOptimization.Description: Stops Windows from using your bandwidth to upload updates to other PCs on the internet or local network.

WPFTweaksRemoveEdge.Description: Uninstalls Microsoft Edge by creating dummy MicrosoftEdge.exe file in the legacy Edge folder. This tricks Windows into unlocking the official Edge uninstaller allowing for a system-level removal.
UndoScript:
Write-Host "Installing Microsoft Edge..."
      winget install Microsoft.Edge --source winget

WPFTweaksUTC.Content: Date & Time - Set Time to UTC
WPFTweaksUTC.Description: Essential for computers that are dual booting. Fixes the time sync with Linux systems.

WPFTweaksRemoveOneDrive.Description: Denies permission to remove OneDrive user files, then uses its own uninstaller to remove it and restores the original permission afterward.
InvokeScript:
# Deny permission to remove OneDrive folder
      icacls $Env:OneDrive /deny "*S-1-5-32-544:(D,DC)"

      Write-Host "Uninstalling OneDrive..."
      Start-Process -FilePath (Join-Path $Env:SystemRoot "System32\OneDriveSetup.exe") -ArgumentList '/uninstall' -Wait

      # Some of OneDrive files use explorer, and OneDrive uses FileCoAuth
      Write-Host "Removing leftover OneDrive Files..."

      Stop-Process -Name FileCoAuth,Explorer

      Remove-Item "$Env:LocalAppData\Microsoft\OneDrive" -Recurse -Force
      Remove-Item "$Env:ProgramData\Microsoft OneDrive" -Recurse -Force

      # Grant back permission to access OneDrive folder
      icacls $Env:OneDrive /grant "*S-1-5-32-544:(D,DC)"

      if (-not (Get-ChildItem -Path $Env:OneDrive)) {
          Remove-Item -Path $Env:OneDrive -Recurse
          [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('OneDrive', $null, 'User')
      }

      # Disable OneSyncSvc
      Set-Service -Name OneSyncSvc -StartupType Disabled
UndoScript:
Write-Host "Installing OneDrive"
      winget install Microsoft.Onedrive --source winget

      # Enabled OneSyncSvc
      Set-Service -Name OneSyncSvc -StartupType Automatic

WPFTweaksRemoveHomeAndGallery.Content: File Explorer Home and Gallery - Disable
WPFTweaksRemoveHomeAndGallery.Description: Removes the Home and Gallery from Explorer and sets This PC as default.

WPFTweaksDisplay.Content: Visual Effects - Set to Best Performance
WPFTweaksDisplay.Description: Sets the system preferences to performance. You can do this manually with sysdm.cpl as well.

WPFTweaksReservedStorage.Description: Disables Windows Reserved Storage (7-10 GB held for updates/temp files). Recommended only on small drives. Re-enable before major Windows feature updates to avoid installation failures.

WPFTweaksRestorePoint.Description: Creates a restore point at runtime in case a revert is needed from WinUtil modifications.

WPFTweaksEndTaskOnTaskbar.Content: End Task With Right Click - Enable
WPFTweaksEndTaskOnTaskbar.Description: Enables option to end task when right-clicking a program in the taskbar.

WPFTweaksStorage.Description: Storage Sense deletes temp files automatically.

WPFTweaksWindowsAI.Description: Removes and disables all AI features/packages
InvokeScript:
$Appx = (Get-AppxPackage MicrosoftWindows.Client.CoreAI).PackageFullName
      $Sid = (Get-LocalUser $Env:UserName).Sid.Value

      New-Item "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Appx\AppxAllUserStore\EndOfLife\$Sid\$Appx" -Force

      Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers "*Copilot*" | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers
      winget uninstall -e --name "Copilot" --silent --force --accept-source-agreements 2>$null
      Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.MicrosoftOfficeHub | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers

      if ($Appx) {
          Remove-AppxPackage $Appx
      }

      Set-Service -Name WSAIFabricSvc -StartupType Disabled
      Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -FeatureName Recall -Online -NoRestart

      Write-Host "Windows AI Disabled"

WPFTweaksWPBT.Description: If enabled, WPBT allows your computer vendor to execute programs at boot time, such as anti-theft software, software drivers, as well as force install software without user consent. Poses potential security risk.

WPFTweaksPreventDeviceMetadataFromNetwor.Description: Prevents additional software from being installed when plugging in devices (e.g. Ads when plugging in a monitor). Poses potential security risk.

WPFTweaksRazerBlock.Description: Blocks ALL Razer Software installations. The hardware works fine without any software.

WPFTweaksLogiBlock.Description: Blocks the Logi Download Assistant that Windows Update keeps reinstalling with Logitech device drivers. Logitech hardware keeps working without it.

WPFTweaksBlockAdobeNet.Description: Reduces user interruptions by selectively blocking connections to Adobe's activation and telemetry servers. Credit: Ruddernation-Designs
InvokeScript:
$hostsUrl = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri https://github.com/Ruddernation-Designs/Adobe-URL-Block-List/raw/refs/heads/master/hosts
      Add-Content -Path "$Env:SystemRoot\System32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Value $hostsUrl

      ipconfig /flushdns
      Write-Host 'Added Adobe url block list from host file'
UndoScript:
Set-Content "$Env:SystemRoot\System32\drivers\etc\hosts" (
          (Get-Content "$Env:SystemRoot\System32\drivers\etc\hosts") -join "`n" -replace '(?s)#New Ver.*', ''
      )

      ipconfig /flushdns
      Write-Host 'Removed Adobe url block list from host file'

WPFTweaksRightClickMenu.Description: Restores the classic context menu when right-clicking in File Explorer, replacing the simplified Windows 11 version.

WPFTweaksDiskCleanup.Description: Runs Disk Cleanup on Drive C: and removes old Windows Updates.

InvokeScript:
# A temp folder always holds files something has open, including this run's own, and
      # the job layer counts a logged error as a failed step
      Remove-Item -Path "$Env:Temp\*" -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
      Remove-Item -Path "$Env:SystemRoot\Temp\*" -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

WPFTweaksIPv46.Description: Setting the IPv4 preference can have latency and security benefits on private networks where IPv6 is not configured.

WPFTweaksTeredo.Description: Teredo network tunneling is an IPv6 feature that can cause additional latency, but may cause problems with some games.
InvokeScript: netsh interface teredo set state disabled
UndoScript: netsh interface teredo set state default

WPFTweaksDisableBGapps.Description: Disables all Microsoft Store apps from running in the background, which has to be done individually since Windows 11.

WPFTweaksDeBloat.Content: Remove ALL MS Store Apps - NOT RECOMMENDED
WPFTweaksDeBloat.Description: High impact: removes a legacy WinUtil list of Microsoft Store apps for all users and deprovisions them for new accounts. This includes Minecraft Bedrock, Gaming Services, media apps, communications apps and some third-party Store apps when present. It does not literally remove every Store app: Microsoft Store and essential frameworks are left alone. No automatic Undo is available; removed apps and games must be reinstalled separately, and some app data may be lost.

WPFTweaksDisableExplorerAutoDiscovery.Content: File Explorer Automatic Folder Discovery - Disable
WPFTweaksDisableExplorerAutoDiscovery.Description: Windows Explorer automatically tries to guess the type of the folder based on its contents, slowing down the browsing experience. WARNING! Will disable File Explorer grouping.
InvokeScript:
# Previously detected folders
      $bags = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags"

      # Folder types lookup table
      $bagMRU = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU"

      # Flush Explorer view database
      Remove-Item -Path $bags -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bags"

      Remove-Item -Path $bagMRU -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bagMRU"

      # Every folder
      $allFolders = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags\AllFolders\Shell"

      if (!(Test-Path $allFolders)) {
        New-Item -Path $allFolders -Force
        Write-Host "Created $allFolders"
      }

      # Generic view
      New-ItemProperty -Path $allFolders -Name "FolderType" -Value "NotSpecified" -PropertyType String -Force
      Write-Host "Set FolderType to NotSpecified"

      Write-Host Please sign out and back in, or restart your computer to apply the changes!
UndoScript:
# Previously detected folders
      $bags = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags"

      # Folder types lookup table
      $bagMRU = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU"

      # Flush Explorer view database
      Remove-Item -Path $bags -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bags"

      Remove-Item -Path $bagMRU -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bagMRU"

      Write-Host Please sign out and back in, or restart your computer to apply the changes!

WPFToggleDetailedBSoD.Description: Gives more information when you blue screen.

WPFToggleBatteryPercentage.Description: Shows numeric battery percentage next to the battery icon in the system tray.

WPFToggleDarkMode.Description: Dark Mode for the system and applications.

WPFToggleNewOutlook.Description: This will ensure the new Outlook application is used.

WPFToggleScrollbars.Description: If enabled, scrollbars will always be visible. If disabled, Windows will automatically hide scrollbars when not in use.

WPFMultiplaneOverlay.Description: Multiplane Overlay composes multiple image layers, which can sometimes cause issues with graphics cards. Changes to this preference are applied immediately.

ComboDescriptions.Disabled (Compatibility): Disables MPO using OverlayTestMode=5, the less aggressive compatibility method.
ComboDescriptions.Fully Disabled: Disables MPO using OverlayTestMode=5 and DisableOverlays=1, the more aggressive method.

WPFToggleMouseAcceleration.Description: Makes it so Cursor movement is affected by the speed of your physical mouse movements.

WPFToggleNumLock.Description: Toggle the Num Lock key state when your computer starts.

WPFToggleWindowSnapping.Description: Toggles the window snapping feature when dragging windows.

WPFToggleStandbyFix.Description: Toggles network connectivity during S0 Sleep which is low power idle in modern laptops.

WPFToggleS3Sleep.Description: Toggles between Modern Standby and S3 Sleep, which cuts off power to the CPU while continuing to refresh the memory.

WPFToggleHideSettingsHome.Description: Toggles the Home Page in the Windows Settings app.

WPFToggleBingSearch.Description: Toggles Bing web search results in Windows Search.

WPFToggleLoginBlur.Description: Toggles the acrylic blur effect on login screen background.

WPFToggleDisableLockscreen.Description: Skips the lock screen entirely and goes directly to the sign-in screen on boot and wake.

WPFToggleStartMenuRecommendations.Description: Toggles the recommendations section in the Start Menu. WARNING: This will also disable Windows Spotlight on your Lock Screen as a side effect.

WPFToggleStickyKeys.Description: Toggles the Sticky Keys, which activate when clicking shift rapidly.

WPFToggleTaskbarAlignment.Description: Toggles the Taskbar alignment either to the left or center.

WPFToggleTaskbarSearch.Description: Toggles the Search Button on the Taskbar.

WPFToggleTaskView.Description: Toggles the Task View Button in the Taskbar.

WPFToggleGameMode.Description: Toggles Windows prioritizes gaming performance by allocating system resources to games.

WPFToggleGameDVR.Description: Toggles Xbox Game Bar background capture (Record what happened). Turning it off avoids continuous video encoding while gaming. Screenshots and manual recording are not removed.

WPFToggleGamingMultimediaProfile.Description: Toggles the MMCSS system profile: reserves 10% CPU for background tasks instead of 20% (SystemResponsiveness) and turns off multimedia network throttling (NetworkThrottlingIndex 0xFFFFFFFF). Turning it off restores the Windows defaults 20 and 10. FPS gains are not guaranteed.

WPFToggleFastStartup.Description: Toggles Fast Startup (HiberbootEnabled). Turning it off makes Shut down perform a full shutdown, so drivers and the kernel start clean; boot can take a few seconds longer. Has no effect while hibernation is disabled.

WPFToggleLongPaths.Description: Toggles support for file paths longer than 260 characters in Explorer.

WPFchangedns.ComboItems: Default DHCP Fastest Google Cloudflare Cloudflare_Malware Cloudflare_Malware_Adult Open_DNS Quad9 AdGuard_Ads_Trackers AdGuard_Ads_Trackers_Malware_Adult
